subject: Regional data custody and failover for private deploys (EU/APAC) — bridging questions
messages:

Cc: Tom Andersson <tom.andersson@nordichealth.se>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:05:12Z
Subject: Regional data custody and failover for Private Deploy - initial questions

Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. A few follow-ups from our security and infra teams as we map SakuraBank's regulatory requirements across EU and APAC private deployments: 

- We need explicit tenant-level placement: can we guarantee that customer A's inference tokens never leave EU primary hosts (including warm standby) unless we explicitly trigger a cross-border failover?
- For warm-standby in APAC: what encryption-forwarding model do you support for customer-managed keys? Can the KMS never leave EU control plane?
- Audit trail: we require per-request audit entries (who, which model version, ingress region, egress region) retained for 3 years. Is that available from the private control plane?

Also attaching our high-level compliance checklist — if you can indicate gaps that would be great.

Best,
Elisa Tan
Head of Cloud Security, SakuraBank
attachments: sakura-checklist.pdf (referenced)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Elisa Tan <elisa.tan@sakurabank.jp>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T12:18:44Z
Subject: Re: Regional data custody and failover for Private Deploy - initial questions

Hi Elisa — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, followed by an action list and attachments.

1) Tenant-level placement guarantee: yes. In Redwood Private we support tenant pinning to a specific region/cluster. Primary and any warm standby for that tenant are deployed into clusters you authorize. Cross-border failover must be explicitly initiated by an admin action (or a policy-based trigger you configure) — we do not perform automatic cross-border evacuation.

2) Customer-managed keys: supported. You can attach a KMS/HSM per-region. The control plane can be configured so key wrapping/decryption operations never leave the EU KMS instance; the APAC warm-standby will store wrapped keys and can only use them when you flip the failover switch. We call this a wrapped-key handoff model.

3) Audit trail and retention: the private control plane produces per-request audit events (token metadata, model version, source IP, region markers). We can configure retention to 3 years in a compliant S3 bucket in your EU tenancy, with immutability flags where required.

I've attached: residency-bridging-arch.pdf (diagram of proposed EU primary / APAC warm-standby topology), tenant-placement-matrix.xlsx (shows placement rules and policy examples), and network-peering-checklist.txt (practical vendorside requirements).

Next steps I propose:
- Technical tabletop next week (60m) to step through a cold failover and a controlled cross-border handoff
- Redline the tenant placement matrix with SakuraBank for final acceptance testing
- Run an audit ingestion sample to validate the 3-year retention write path

Proposed slots: Tue 2026-12-22 09:00-10:00 UTC or Thu 2026-12-24 14:00-15:00 UTC. Zoom link in Drive doc.

Onward,
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: residency-bridging-arch.pdf, tenant-placement-matrix.xlsx, network-peering-checklist.txt

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elisa Tan <elisa.tan@sakurabank.jp>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T14:06:07Z
Subject: Re: Regional data custody and failover for Private Deploy - initial questions

Elisa — adding a few operational constraints from the runtime and networking side: 

- Control plane split: to meet strict EU-only key usage we recommend a dual-controlplane model where the EU control plane holds key material and the APAC control plane operates in a "standby-only" mode until an explicit failover. This removes the risk of accidental key usage outside EU.
- KV cache handling: during failover a warmed KV cache can be restored but only if customer consents to copying encrypted cache blobs to the standby region. We log that consent event.
- BGP peering & egress IPs: per our network-peering-checklist, we will publish a static egress block for your tenancy in each region; if you need egress IP whitelisting, that can be done per-tenant.
- RTO/RPO targets: for warm standby we typically hit RTO ~ 2–6 mins for stateless workloads and RTO ~ 10–20 mins if cache restoration is required; RPO is configurable (near-zero with synchronous replication, or up to a few minutes with async).

I'll capture these as constraints in the shared Drive doc. Hoping to align on the exact RTO requirement so we can finalize the acceptance test.

—Marcus
Senior PM, Runtime Performance

Also, can we schedule a tabletop where we simulate a region-boundary failover initiated by SakuraBank security, and one initiated by Redwood (operator-assisted) to validate approvals? Prefer Dec 23 09:30-10:30 UTC if that works.

Regards,

- Audit export to partner archive: supported. We can stream a filtered audit feed (metadata only) to your partner's archive endpoint. We support schema-level filtering so PII and key identifiers are suppressed; a cryptographic digest can be included for traceability without revealing key material.

- Tabletop: Dec 23 09:30-10:30 UTC works for us. We'll use the Drive Zoom link (https://zoom.us/j/9876543210). Agenda: 1) Walk the EU primary -> APAC warm-standby failover, 2) Demonstrate wrapped-key handoff, 3) Validate audit export and retention pipeline, 4) Acceptance checklist run.

- Prepare sample audit export and push to partner archive (Marcus / due 2026-12-22)
